# Alice AI — hash-pinned dependency lock (HIGH-3, deep-security-audit).
#
# Every dependency is pinned to an EXACT version AND its artifact SHA-256
# hash(es). Build/install the signed release with hash enforcement so the
# bundle can only contain these exact artifacts — a yanked / compromised /
# typosquatted re-resolve fails closed:
#
#     pip install --require-hashes -r backend/requirements.lock.txt
#   (or)
#     uv pip sync --require-hashes backend/requirements.lock.txt
#
# Provenance: generated from the verified dev venv (.venv, Python 3.12) via
#   pip freeze --exclude-editable | uv pip compile --generate-hashes
# so the locked versions are exactly what the audited environment ran.
#
# NOT INCLUDED (install separately, by design):
#   * alice_acp — our Track-A inference engine, now VENDORED in-repo under
#     backend/vendor/ (see ../NOTICE §2). It is first-party source, not a PyPI
#     artifact, so it is not hash-pinned here; install it separately as a path
#     package: `cd backend && pip install --no-deps ./vendor`. Its two import-time
#     deps (SQLAlchemy + cryptography, and their C-deps cffi/pycparser) ARE pinned
#     below, so --no-deps is safe.
#
# Platform note: mlx/mlx-metal/mlx-lm are Apple-Silicon wheels (the macOS
# target). Regenerate this lock per packaged platform (e.g. a CUDA/llama.cpp
# Windows/Linux build resolves different accelerator wheels).
#
# Regenerate after a dependency change:
#   .venv/bin/pip freeze --exclude-editable | grep -viE '^alice[-_]acp' > /tmp/f.txt
#   uv pip compile --generate-hashes --no-annotate --no-header /tmp/f.txt \
#       -o backend/requirements.lock.txt   # then re-prepend this header
#   (the `alice[-_]acp` filter drops the vendored path package — it is installed
#    separately via `pip install --no-deps ./vendor`, not from this lock.)
